I am still declining on one blocking domain error. Step 2, lines 147-148: "**Did both sides finish?** A side with no pass marker was truncated, so every \"removed\" line after the truncation point is an artefact of the kill, not a behaviour change." Absence of a pass marker means the run did not reach a clean end — it does NOT mean the run was truncated. The most common cause is that the run genuinely failed, which is this skill's own headline trigger: the description advertises "when a customer testcase passes on the old build and fails on the new one". In exactly that case the candidate side has no pass marker because it failed, and step 2 instructs a junior to write off every subsequent removed line as an artefact of a kill — discarding precisely the evidence the comparison exists to find. Only a kill, timeout or infra abort makes the tail an artefact.

It compounds twice. The step 2 Grep alternates only the banner, the profile's Run identity and the profile's Pass marker; the skill never spends the profile's **Fatal markers** or **Infra markers** and does not list them among its pack-wide facts, so the procedure structurally cannot separate "ran to a real failure" from "was killed" — yet the step asserts one reading. And `completion : <which side carried the pass marker, and which did not>` is the only completion field, so the report has no way to record the distinction even if the engineer makes it. This is also the one assertion about the reader's flow that is neither a slot nor derivable from the profile.

I could not distinguish pre-existing from newly-introduced defects: the directory is untracked (`?? skills/dv-tool-release-behaviour-diff/`) with no prior committed version to diff against, so new_problems is left empty rather than guessed.
remaining: BLOCKER — step 2 (lines 147-148): "A side with no pass marker was truncated, so every 'removed' line after the truncation point is an artefact of the kill, not a behaviour change." A missing pass marker means the run did not reach a clean end, not that it was truncated. In the skill's own advertised case ("a customer testcase passes on the old build and fails on the new one") the candidate side has no pass marker because it FAILED, and the tail is the behaviour change, not a kill artefact. Split the three causes (real failure / kill or timeout / infra abort), spend the profile's Fatal markers and Infra markers to tell them apart (add both to the pack-wide facts table and to the step 2 alternation — the Grep count does not change), and widen `completion` so it can say 'finished with a failure' as distinct from 'was killed'.

The degraded no-comparison-file path is fully costed at steps 1 and 3 (budget rule 4 even prices it at eleven Greps) and then stops being specified. Step 5 — the only step that opens content — is written purely in hunk terms ("Spend the six windowed Reads on hunks that look unlike each other", "the first hunk, the last, and four from regions whose surrounding text differs"); budget rule 5's 200-hunk ceiling is hunk-only; and the mandatory coverage line and its worked example are hunk-only ("6 of 214 hunks opened"). On the marker-only path there are no hunks, so a junior reaches step 5 and the coverage line with no vocabulary that fits. Steps 7 and 8 leave the same cluster with two legal classifications, in the step that opens by promising "two engineers classifying the same cluster write the same field". For clusters ranked 4-6 (half the possible output, since six Reads cap you at six clusters) the notes were never searched: the regression basis rule ("Name any of those that was not searched, and why") permits `regression`, while the unclassified basis rule, whose own example is budget exhaustion ("hunk not opened, the six Reads were spent"), points to `unclassified`. Pick one and say it.

Budget rule 4 says "two Greps of the tool component owner map in step 9", but step 9 says `class` decides which map and that a `class: design` cluster's owner comes from the profile's Area-to-owner map — which the pack-wide facts table confirms is spent at step 9. The count of two still holds; the budget line names only one of the two files those Greps can land in. Reword to 'two Greps of whichever owner map step 9 selects'.
